[Zaptruder] The magic of being 10-15 years behind in understanding the global market.
They've taken all the good ideas. They've established their own manufacturing, design and production companies. They're racing ahead continuing to make stuff at break neck pace because they have a huge domestic and global market and the supply chain to put it together faster then everyone else, and the ability to prove out the ideas more easily with the larger market and iterate faster and see what sticks.
This is what happens when the rest of the planet sends their work to one place to get it made cheaply. The don't just 'copy the homework' they learn from it and improve on it.
[MrFrugalSpend] It started out as reverse engineering. However now they have gone way beyond that. Half dozen delegates from my company just came back from a trade expo in China - very impressed. One said yesterday, 'we are getting left so behind guys' (as in the whole country / west). One of my managers then required me to drop our local procurement plans and investigate offshore sourcing from there because we will get so much better quality (for the money). Our competitors are doing it - we kind of have to despite not liking what it means for Australia. It's no longer a conversation about cheap alternatives - it's about the best / best value products.

[MrFrugalSpend] Oh no, at least when you go commando you can wash your pants - but you rock "commandtoe" by raw-dogging enclosed running shoes!?
I'll give you the ai slop answer:
Your feet contain over 250,000 sweat glands that release substantial moisture daily. Socks absorb this sweat before it soaks directly into your footwear. When sweat stays trapped against bare skin inside a dark, warm shoe, it creates an ideal breeding ground for odour-causing bacteria and fungi. Clean socks reduce these risks, helping to prevent conditions like athlete's foot and stubborn foot odour. They also act as a buffer to minimises direct friction, preventing painful blisters, chafing, and skin irritation…
Don't even get me started about having your shoe laces too loose for running (these are runners after all)…
…maybe you'd be better to get machine washable Skechers slip-ins - they are made for your use-case (and throw them in the wash regularly)
